sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a neutral pose, showing the card face of the tabard. Panel 2: full-body true side profile, showing how thin and flat the card tabard is. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the card-back pattern of the tabard. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, face clearly lit under the cap. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the cap to the soles of the boots with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: ONE background gardener of the Queen of Hearts' rose-garden, alone on the sheet: a man about 40 years old, a real human actor with an ordinary working build, about 172 cm tall. Weathered outdoor face, short brown hair flecked with grey under the cap, grey-blue eyes, quiet eyes-down working demeanour. He reads oblong and flat like a playing card: the rigid card tabard makes a flat rectangle of his body, with his arms and legs emerging at its four corners. His dress follows the group rule, quoted verbatim from the costume bible: 'background 1862 estate gardeners dressed as playing cards of the club suit: stiff flat oblong card tabards hanging front and back to the knee, ivory fronts with black club pips and corner rank indices, backs in a crimson-and-cream lattice card-back pattern with a small heart rosette, over crimson wool working shirt-sleeves and crimson breeches, cream stockings, brown boots and flat brown cloth caps; working-worn, a little earth and paint'. On this one gardener that means he is the Four of Clubs: the ivory card front carries exactly four large black club pips, one in each corner of the pip field, and a small '4' index with a small club in the top-left and bottom-right corners; plain flat brown cloth cap with no badge, no brass buttons. He holds a plain zinc watering can in one hand.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate panels side by side, exactly one gardener in each panel, the same man in front / side / back full-body views and one head-and-shoulders close-up.
